title: Build a Responsive Navbar with Flexbox
description: Create a navigation bar that uses flex properties for layout and alignment.
problemStatement:
Write the HTML and CSS for a responsive navigation bar. Structure:
- A `<nav>` with class `navbar`.
- Inside, a `<div class="brand">` containing the text "Progly".
- An unordered list `<ul class="nav-menu">` with three links: Home, Courses, Contact.

**CSS requirements:**
- Use `display: flex;` on `.navbar`.
- Align items vertically centred (`align-items: center;`).
- Use `justify-content: space-between;` to push brand to left and menu to right.
- Style the `.nav-menu` also as a flex container to lay out list items horizontally.
- Remove default list styling (`list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0;`).
- Add a gap of 1.5rem between menu items.
- Add some padding (1rem) and a background colour to the navbar.
- On screens smaller than 600px, change the navbar to `flex-direction: column;` and centre the brand and menu (`align-items: center;`). Use a media query.

Provide the full HTML (just the nav part, assume inside a body) and CSS. The CSS should include the global box‑sizing reset and the media query.
hints: For the media query, use `@media (max-width: 600px) { .navbar { flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } }`.
The brand can just be a `<div>`, no special class needed for styles beyond maybe `font-weight`.
Don't forget to use `gap` or `margin` to space the links.
expectedOutput: A working navbar that displays horizontally on desktop and stacks vertically on mobile with centred content.
